## Brief
OP's main point was To critique and debunk the claims made in the "How Money Works" YouTube video. The dominant replies focused on Critique of "How Money Works" Channel Quality. Consensus stayed around critique of "how money works" channel quality while impact of regulations. Dissent centered on The OP's choice of "population 16+" for homes per capita might inflate.

## Detailed
## OP Intent
- To endorse and amplify the claims made in the "How Money Works" YouTube video titled "jUsT BUiLd MorE hOusEs!!" regarding the US housing market, specifically its assertions about housing supply, affordability, and construction productivity. ## Reply Clusters
- Critique of "How Money Works" Channel Quality: Many commenters express a general distrust or disappointment with the "How Money Works" channel, describing it as narrative-driven, lacking research, and catering to audience biases rather than providing accurate economic analysis.
- Impact of Regulations and Policy on Housing Costs: Several commenters highlight how government regulations, zoning laws, development fees, and specific policies (e.g., anti-landlord measures, elevator regulations) significantly drive up construction costs and reduce housing supply, often with counterproductive results.
- Nuances of Construction Costs and Productivity: While generally agreeing with the OP that construction costs are a problem, some commenters elaborate on the specific drivers of these costs, distinguishing between artificial (regulatory) and productivity-related factors, and noting regional differences.
- Data Interpretation and Metrics for Housing Supply: Commenters discuss the appropriate metrics for assessing housing supply, questioning the OP's choice of "population 16+" and offering alternative data points or interpretations.
- Generational Anxiety and Economic Outlook: One comment expresses concern about the economic future for Gen Z, particularly in the context of housing affordability, reflecting broader anxieties. ### Critique of "How Money Works" Channel Quality
- I've realized that how money works is not an economics channel. It is a series of narratives and just-so stories based on vibes. No citations, no references, just opinions stated as if they were unquestionable well-known facts.
- ive watched a few of his videos. i get the sense he was a finance guy who pivoted to covering broader economy stuff. The issue is that he's putting out like one video per week on a relatively broad number of topics. There's not really a way for him to be an expert in all of what he covers, and he doesn't give himself enough time to research stuff.
- HMW is someone who couldn't make it in IB, so he saw an opportunity in YouTubing. Knowing that fact, it makes a whole lot of sense now. Dude couldn't make it in a field that requires good and accurate research, so he jumps to a field that doesn't necessarily need it… And arguably rewards you for bad research.
- The most ironically named channel on YouTube
- Not surprising at all that How Money Works made a video that is wrong. That's what that channel does. ### Impact of Regulations and Policy on Housing Costs
- This kind of talk can drive even more dysfunctional housing policy - in the UK we have the exact same problem for the exact same reason. However, here a few years ago the government, rather than address the real problem, introduced a series of "f*** landlords" policies. This has had the horribly predictable consequence of landlords leaving the market in droves and rents skyrocketing…
- Ireland has been running rent caps and rent pressure zones for fucking years now and its destroyed our housing market and yet the opposition parties proposed solution. is. stricter rent caps.
- Wanna build a single-family house in Toronto? $137,846 in permitting fees please! A multi family 2+ bedroom unit? $113,938 please!
- Fees are on average $29,000 per unit in California, up to >100K, 10 to 40x what it costs in Texas.
- I think the biggest drivers of high housing costs are legal: zoning that drives up the price of land and legal battles to build anything new.
- I've been in this industry for 30 years and I think the main things driving up costs are increased regulation and stricter codes, rising labor costs due to a shortage of skilled labor, and rising materials costs. ### Nuances of Construction Costs and Productivity
- I'm actually somewhat sympathetic to the construction cost argument, but I think we need to separate the overall "housing market" into a few different markets.
- Costs are an issue, but I think they're mostly artificial costs, not productivity-related. I would love to see some research quantifying this, but I think the biggest drivers of high housing costs are legal: zoning that drives up the price of land and legal battles to build anything new.
- My general senses are the following. 1. There are large differences in cost *levels* across space (Houston vs San Francisco) 2. Where there are large differences in cost *changes*, these tend to be because one place has gotten more expensive, not because another place has gotten cheaper.
- Houston isn't actually able to build apartments when rents are $1,600 a month, when so many others don't seem to be able to build them unless rents are $3,000 a month, because of our magical hammer swingers or anything else having to do with "productivity". ### Data Interpretation and Metrics for Housing Supply
- Why use 16+? I don't know anyone who moved at 16 and college dorms aren't counted in housing stock. Don't we have numbers for the estimated total # of households in the US?
- The FRED has units/household and units/population numbers already charted, both of which show positive signs: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/?g=ScEE https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/?g=j9kH#
- But you're significantly inflating your denominator by using 16+, so it's hard to evaluate the argument when a key measurement relies on convenient data rather than appropriate data. Reducing the denominator to 18+ or 25+ wouldn't make HMW's numbers look worse - it would make yours look less favorable to your shortage argument. ### Generational Anxiety and Economic Outlook
- can someone please tell me that Gen Z isn't screwed? I'm about to blackpill with all the people online bitching about everything.
- We'll be fine. I love the Taylor Tomlinson bit about self-pep-talks looking in the mirror saying "I'm gonna make it today… because what other goddamn choice I have?" Just be. And unplug from larger narratives like "the economy", "the government", or "social justice" and others until you're equipped to make a change. ## Counterarguments
- The OP's choice of "population 16+" for homes per capita might inflate the denominator, potentially making the housing shortage argument appear stronger than if 18+ or 25+ adults were used, as it includes individuals less likely to form independent households.
- While the OP critiques HMW's specific argument about private equity's impact on HVAC costs, some commenters agree with the general premise that construction costs are a significant issue, even if the specific mechanism proposed by HMW is flawed or overblown.
- The OP's example of destroyed housing stock leading to a relatively fixed ratio of housing units to households might overlook that many affected households would relocate entirely, creating new household formations elsewhere and thus impacting the ratio in other regions.
- The OP's assertion that "luxury" apartments are affordable to families making 80% of the area's median income, while supported by some data, may not align with the lived experience of many renters who perceive new construction as prohibitively expensive.
- The OP's focus on national vacancy rates being near historical lows, while valid, does not fully address the point that there *are* empty homes, just not in desirable areas, which represents a different kind of "shortage" for those seeking housing in specific, high-demand locations. ## Unresolved Questions
- How much of the increase in construction costs is due to artificial (regulatory/legal) factors versus genuine productivity stagnation, and what is the precise quantification of each?
- What is the most appropriate demographic denominator (e.g., 16+, 18+, 25+, or households) for accurately measuring homes per capita/adult, and how does the choice of metric affect the perception and analysis of housing supply?
- To what extent do local micro-monopolies (e.g., private equity buying HVAC and plumbing companies) actually impact overall construction costs and productivity, and is there concrete evidence beyond anecdotal or plausible claims?
- How can policy effectively address the housing crisis and promote affordability without resorting to counterproductive measures like strict rent caps or punitive taxes on landlords, which have been shown to worsen supply and affordability in some markets?
- What are the specific, actionable solutions to improve construction productivity and reduce building costs, considering the historical challenges and the interplay of technology, labor, and regulation? ## Moderation Context
- Rendered comments covered only part of the thread (25/112 visible; divergence 77.68%).

## Brief
This summary details the publication history, online availability, and structural organization of Karl Marx's *Capital: A Critique of Political Economy, Volume One*. It covers the original German and English editions, the specifics of the Marx/Engels Internet Archive version, available digital formats, and the book's eight-part structure with key chapter titles and additional content.

## Detailed
## Publication Details
- First published in German in 1869.
- First English edition published in 1885.
- Online version from marxists.org is based on the 1887 English edition.
- English translation by Samuel Moore and Edward Aveling.
- Edited by Frederick Engels.
- Includes changes from the 4th German edition.

## Brief
An investigation by Bellingcat and Cerosetenta links Colombian politician and businessman Jorge Rodriguez to the neo-Nazi group Active Club Bogota through video evidence, social media interactions, and shared activities, despite Rodriguez's denials and legal threats. The report details Active Club Bogota's international connections and activities, and the potential implications of such affiliations.

## Detailed
## Investigation Findings
- Bellingcat and Colombian media outlet Cerosetenta linked Colombian politician and businessman Jorge Rodriguez to the neo-Nazi group Active Club Bogota.
- A video from February 26 shows Rodriguez and other men painting over graffiti in Buenos Aires's Restrepo neighborhood.
- Rodriguez claimed on Instagram they were 'defending public space to stop generating hatred', but they covered a message reading, 'Creole Nazis will not pass.' ## Evidence Linking Rodriguez to Active Club Bogota
- A pixelated man in the video has tattoos with multiple similarities to Javier "Orlik" Ruiz, a prominent member of Active Club Bogota.
- Bellingcat identified Ruiz by matching tattoos on his hands, fingers (including an arrow on his left middle finger), and arms from unpixelated frames with numerous public photos.
- Rodriguez follows Ruiz on Instagram.
- Ruiz 'liked' the video posted by Rodriguez.
- Active Club Bogota's official Instagram account is one of just over 60 accounts that follows Rodriguez.
- In March, Rodriguez also 'liked' a March 2026 post from the group featuring a neo-Nazi movement flag. ## Active Club Bogota Profile and Activities
- Active Club Bogota has been online since early 2024.
- It is the only official South American chapter of the international network started by US white supremacist Robert Rundo.
- The network uses fitness and fighting to recruit young men.
- The Bogota chapter hosted Adolf Hitler birthday celebrations at a community centre in 2025 (with a book burning) and 2026 (with swastika cupcakes and a 1940 Nazi propaganda film). ## Political Context and Reactions
- Rodriguez unsuccessfully ran for congress in the March 2026 elections with the Centro Democratico party, receiving 4,401 votes.
- He presents himself as a prominent Centro Democratico member and has appeared with party figures including Rafael Nieto Loaiza, Gabriel Vallejo, Paloma Valencia, and Alvaro Uribe Velez.
- Centro Democratico's National Director stated the party was unaware of any proven links and does not endorse groups that incite hate.
- Experts Alexander Ritzmann (CEP) and Heidi Beirich (GPAHE) warned that such affiliations lend legitimacy to neo-Nazi groups and that even small chapters can be recruitment hubs for transnational networks. ## Legal Responses and Journalistic Justification
- Both Rodriguez and Ruiz responded to Bellingcat's queries with legal threats, citing Colombian data protection laws, but did not answer questions.
- Bellingcat and Cerosetenta consulted legal experts and determined their reporting is protected by freedom of expression.
- They cited public interest and the subjects' status as 'public figures' as justification for their reporting. ## International Neo-Nazi Network Links
- The investigation suggests Active Club Bogota has links to international neo-Nazi networks Blood & Honour and Combat 18.
- There is no evidence connecting Rodriguez directly to Blood & Honour or Combat 18.
- Evidence includes a May 2024 photo of a man with Ruiz's tattoos next to Blood & Honour musician Ken McLellan in Bogota.
- Another associate sent gifts (including an Active Club Bogota sticker) to the alleged leader of Combat 18 in Spain.
- A neo-Nazi fashion retailer listing Ruiz as a contact was banned from WhatsApp by Meta after Bellingcat reached out.
- Combat 18 is designated a terrorist organization in Canada and is subject to UK financial sanctions.

## OP Intent
- Ray Dalio, founder of Bridgewater Associates, hosted an Ask Me Anything (AMA) to share his principles on how reality works, life, work, economics, and investments. He also aimed to discuss his views on capitalism reform and promote his educational videos and articles. ## Reply Clusters
- Implementing Radical Transparency and Thoughtful Disagreement: Achieving radical transparency in the workplace requires clear, agreed-upon principles for interaction. Thoughtful disagreement is essential for stress-testing ideas, overcoming biases, and making idea-meritocratic decisions, even when principles conflict or trust is an issue.
- Economic Cycles, Monetary Policy, and Future Outlook: When traditional monetary policies (Monetary Policy 1) become ineffective due to low interest rates, central banks resort to printing money and buying assets (Monetary Policy 2), which can widen wealth gaps. In future downturns, Monetary Policy 3 (government deficits monetized by central banks) will likely be necessary. The combination of ineffective monetary policy and increased societal polarity will lead to surprising outcomes, reminiscent of the 1930s. Amateur investing is highly challenging due to the zero-sum nature of markets.
- Humility and Continuous Personal Growth: Overcoming arrogance and embracing humility is crucial for personal and intellectual growth, enabling one to learn from mistakes and seek out diverse perspectives. Life is a continuous adventure of learning, where passion drives effort, but significant 'grinding' is often required to achieve goals. Principles are constantly refined through experience and reflection.
- The Nature of Wealth and True Happiness: Extraordinary wealth is often a byproduct of passionately building something valuable for many people, rather than a direct pursuit of money. Beyond basic comfort, money does not correlate with happiness; instead, meaningful work, meaningful relationships, and being part of a community are the primary drivers of well-being. - Using thoughtful disagreement to move past biased perspectives towards optimal collective decisions. ### Economic Cycles, Monetary Policy, and Future Outlook

- Emphasizing the need for individuals to adapt to inevitable changes over the next 30 years. ### Utilizing Personality Assessments and Broadening Education

- What are Ray Dalio's thoughts about the subreddit r/wallstreetbets? ## Moderation Context

In this commentary, the interviewer argues that Mark Manson is wrong; Manson responds that the modern pursuit of happiness is counterproductive, as true life satisfaction (eudaimonia) stems from embracing struggle and finding purpose, rather than chasing fleeting hedonic pleasures.

## Detailed
## Overview
- In this commentary, Mark Manson argues that mark manson argues that the modern pursuit of happiness is often counterproductive, as true life satisfaction (eudaimonia) stems from embracing struggle and finding purpose, rather than chasing fleeting hedonic pleasures. ### Format and speakers
- Format: Commentary.
- Speakers: Mark Manson. ### Core argument
- Mark Manson argues that the modern pursuit of happiness is often counterproductive, as true life satisfaction (eudaimonia) stems from embracing struggle and finding purpose, rather than chasing fleeting hedonic pleasures. He proposes that adopting an adult mindset, grounded in unconditional values and virtue ethics, leads to lasting fulfillment. ## Chapter walkthrough ### Happiness vs. Meaning
- Mark Manson argues that happiness is overrated and often backfires when pursued directly.
- He distinguishes between comfort and highs (hedonia) and true life satisfaction (eudaimonia).
- The modern world is optimized for hedonic experiences, such as dopamine hits.
- Eudaimonia, a deeper sense of purpose, is identified as the true driver of satisfaction.
- Manson suggests that people often confuse temporary pleasure with lasting fulfillment. ### The Backwards Law
- Manson cites Alan Watts' "backwards law", stating that chasing positive experiences creates negative ones.
- Conversely, accepting negative experiences can lead to positive outcomes.
- Examples include trying to impress others making one feel less impressive, or desiring more money making one feel poorer.
- Modern marketing often exacerbates this by selling self-perception benefits, promoting an endless chase.
- Meaning and happiness are presented as side effects of embracing purposeful struggles, not direct achievements. ### The Specialness Affliction
- Manson critiques the modern affliction of feeling "special and unique", which he believes breeds entitlement.
- He attributes this phenomenon to two main causes.
- One cause is well-intentioned parents who, based on outdated self-esteem research, inadvertently raised narcissistic children.
- The second cause is the personalized nature of the internet, which curates content reinforcing individual specialness.
- Manson differentiates between grandiose narcissists (feeling superior) and vulnerable narcissists (feeling like unique victims).
- Both types of narcissism ultimately result in selfish demands and expectations. ### Self-Help Limitations
- Manson argues that conventional self-help methods, such as affirmations and visualizations, are often ineffective.
- Research indicates that such techniques can make people with low self-esteem feel more pathetic.
- The underlying issue is that these methods often reinforce the chase for external validation or superficial happiness.
- A deeper, more fundamental shift in mindset is required for genuine personal growth. ### Stages of Maturity
- Drawing on Piaget and Kohlberg, Manson proposes a three-stage model of maturity: Childhood, Adolescence, and Adulthood.
- The Childhood stage is characterized by transactional desires and wanting things.
- The Adolescent stage involves bartering for social status and living conditionally.
- Manson suggests many individuals remain stuck in the fragile adolescent stage.
- The Adult stage is defined by living unconditionally based on core values, even if it means being disliked.
- This adult mindset is described as anti-fragile, gaining strength and wisdom from setbacks and failures. ### Virtue Ethics & Fulfillment
- Manson concludes that his framework rediscovers Aristotle's virtue ethics.
- By prioritizing timeless virtues, individuals can achieve an unconditional way of living.
- This approach allows one to gain strength and insight from failures.
- It leads to lasting fulfillment, contrasting with the hedonic treadmill of chasing temporary highs.
- Embracing virtue ethics fosters an anti-fragile existence where challenges contribute to growth. ## Demonstrations
- Examples illustrating Alan Watts' 'backwards law', such as trying to impress people making one feel less impressive.
- Analogies differentiating grandiose and vulnerable narcissism.
- A three-stage model of maturity (Childhood, Adolescence, Adulthood) to explain personal development. ## Closing remarks
- Recap: By prioritizing timeless virtues and embracing an adult mindset, one can live unconditionally, gain from failure, and find lasting fulfillment, thereby avoiding the superficial pursuit of temporary hedonic highs. This approach fosters an anti-fragile existence where challenges contribute to personal growth.

- Modern encryption, such as RSA-2048, relies on the classical difficulty of factoring large numbers into prime factors.
- A classical supercomputer would take millions of years to break RSA-2048, but a quantum computer could do it in hours. ### Quantum Progress and Cryptographic Vulnerability

- The analogy suggests that struggle in human endeavors arises from internal turbulence, not the task itself.
- Forcing movement paradoxically creates more resistance, mirroring physical turbulence.

- Psychological turbulence is identified as having three primary sources that make simple tasks feel difficult.

- Fear Action, actions driven by avoidance and anxiety, constitutes the third source, remedied by grounded action.
- Removing these sources can significantly enhance the effectiveness of effort.
- Ease is defined as alignment, not complacency, and is experienced during peak performance flow states.

## Brief
Import AI newsletter #455 reports a 60%+ probability that AI systems will autonomously develop their own successors by late 2028, achieving no-human-involved AI R&D. The issue, aimed at those tracking AI capabilities, bases this on public data and aggregate benchmark trends, despite individual benchmark flaws. It details AI's rapid advancements in coding, complex task completion, and scientific R&D skills.

## Detailed
## Overview
- Import AI newsletter #455 reports on recent trends in AI capability research. ### Publication
- Import AI newsletter #455. ### Stance
- The piece adopts a cautionary stance. ### Core argument
- AI systems will be able to autonomously build their own successors—achieving no-human-involved AI R&D—by the end of 2028, with a 60%+ probability. ## Section walkthrough ### The Core Prediction and its Basis
- The author of Import AI newsletter #455 reluctantly posits a 60%+ probability that AI systems will be able to autonomously build their own successors by the end of 2028.
- This prediction implies achieving no-human-involved AI R&D, a milestone in AI development.
- The conclusion is based on public data from sources like arXiv, bioRxiv, and NBER, focusing on the aggregate trend across multiple benchmarks.
- The author acknowledges individual flaws in these benchmarks but emphasizes the overall upward trajectory of AI capabilities.
- A proof-of-concept for a non-frontier model training its successor is expected within a year or two, though full automation is not anticipated in 2026.
- The author's 2028 prediction is tempered by the belief that some human creativity is still needed, with the probability for 2027 stated as 30%.
- If automation does not occur by 2028, it may indicate a fundamental limitation in the current AI paradigm. ### Evidence from Coding and Complex Task Completion
- Evidence for this trend includes AI's rapidly improving capabilities in coding and completing complex, long-duration tasks.
- On the SWE-Bench for real-world GitHub issues, performance has dramatically increased from approximately 2% by Claude 2 in late 2023 to 93.9% by Claude Mythos Preview, effectively saturating the benchmark.
- METR's time horizons plot, which measures the duration of tasks an AI can be 50% reliable at, shows capabilities increasing significantly.
- Capabilities have risen from approximately 30 seconds for GPT-3.5 (2022) to approximately 12 hours for Opus 4.6 (2026).
- Forecaster Ajeya Cotra suggests that approximately 100-hour tasks are possible by the end of 2026.
- These advances correlate with the rise of agentic tools, which allow researchers to delegate tasks such as data cleaning and experiment launching to AI. ### AI Mastering Core Scientific Skills for R&D
- AI is also demonstrating mastery of core scientific skills for its own research and development.
- On CORE-Bench, which tests the reproduction of scientific papers, performance jumped from approximately 21.5% in September 2024 (GPT-4o) to 95.5% in December 2025 (Opus 4.5).
- OpenAI's MLE-Bench, designed for Kaggle competitions, saw scores rise from 16.9% in October 2024 (o1 model) to 64.4% in February 2026 (Gemini3).
- These benchmarks indicate AI's growing ability to understand, replicate, and contribute to scientific processes.
- The rapid improvement across these diverse scientific tasks suggests a foundational shift in AI's capacity for independent research. ### AI in Core AI Development Tasks and Meta-Skills
- In kernel optimization, a core AI development task, AI is now used competitively for tasks like generating Triton kernels at Meta and writing kernels for Huawei's Ascend chips.
- On PostTrainBench, which tests fine-tuning smaller models, AI systems like Opus 4.6 and GPT 5.4 achieve scores of 25%-28%, about half the human baseline of 51% as of March/April 2026.
- In an Anthropic task for optimizing LLM training code, speedups increased from 2.9x (Opus 4, May 2025) to 52x (Claude Mythos Preview, April 2026), where a human takes 4-8 hours for a 4x speedup.
- Anthropic has also shown a proof-of-concept where AI agents autonomously developed techniques for an AI safety problem that beat a human baseline.
- Furthermore, AI systems are developing meta-skills, such as managing other AI agents in synthetic teams, indicating coordination capabilities. ### Creativity, Frontier Lab Pursuit, and Profound Implications
- While the author believes AI cannot yet produce radical, paradigm-shifting ideas like the transformer architecture, they argue that most AI progress is methodical engineering work, which AI is becoming adept at automating.
- There are preliminary signs of creativity in math and computer science, such as a Gemini model finding an interesting solution to an Erdos problem and contributing substantially to a new math proof, though these could be exceptions.
- The author concludes that AI can automate vast swathes of AI engineering today, moving beyond mere task execution to active development.
- This goal is explicitly pursued by frontier labs like OpenAI (aiming for an 'automated AI research intern' by September 2026), Anthropic, and DeepMind, as well as heavily funded startups like Recursive Superintelligence ($500m raised) and Mirendil.
- The implications include urgent alignment challenges, as current techniques could fail under recursive self-improvement, with risks like 'faking alignment' and compounding errors (e.g., a 99.9% accurate method degrading to 60.5% after 500 generations).
- Other consequences are a massive productivity multiplier across the economy, creating issues of access inequality and systemic bottlenecks, and the rise of a capital-heavy, human-light 'machine economy' that poses challenges to inequality and governance. ## Closing remarks
- Call to action: The newsletter also discusses the pursuit of this goal by frontier labs and the, urgent implications for alignment and the economy, noting that some human creativity is still believed necessary.

The report details Active Club Bogota's international connections and activities, and the potential implications of such affiliations.

## Detailed
## Investigation Findings
- Bellingcat and Colombian media outlet Cerosetenta published a piece on activity in Bogota's Restrepo neighborhood.
- A video from February 26 shows Rodriguez and other men painting over graffiti in Bogota's Restrepo neighborhood.
- Rodriguez claimed on Instagram they were 'defending public space to stop generating hatred', but they covered a message reading, 'Creole Nazis will not pass.' ## Evidence Linking Rodriguez to Active Club Bogota
- A pixelated man in the video has tattoos with multiple similarities to Javier "Orlik" Ruiz, a prominent member of Active Club Bogota.
- Bellingcat identified Ruiz by matching tattoos on his hands, fingers (including an arrow on his left middle finger), and arms from unpixelated frames with numerous public photos.
- Rodriguez follows Ruiz on Instagram.
- Ruiz 'liked' the video posted by Rodriguez.
- Active Club Bogota's official Instagram account is one of just over 60 accounts that follows Rodriguez.
- In March, Rodriguez also 'liked' a March 2026 post from the group featuring a neo-Nazi movement flag. ## Active Club Bogota Profile and Activities
- Active Club Bogota has been online since early 2024.
- It is the only official South American chapter of the international network started by US white supremacist Robert Rundo.
- The network uses fitness and fighting to recruit young men.
- The Bogota chapter hosted Adolf Hitler birthday celebrations at a community centre in 2025 (with a book burning) and 2026 (with swastika cupcakes and a 1940 Nazi propaganda film). ## Political Context and Reactions
- Rodriguez unsuccessfully ran for congress in the March 2026 elections with the Centro Democratico party, receiving 4,401 votes.
- He presents himself as a prominent Centro Democratico member and has appeared with party figures including Rafael Nieto Loaiza, Gabriel Vallejo, Paloma Valencia, and Alvaro Uribe Velez.
- Centro Democratico's National Director stated the party was unaware of any proven links and does not endorse groups that incite hate.
- Experts Alexander Ritzmann (CEP) and Heidi Beirich (GPAHE) warned that such affiliations lend legitimacy to neo-Nazi groups and that even small chapters can be recruitment hubs for transnational networks. ## Legal Responses and Journalistic Justification
- Both Rodriguez and Ruiz responded to Bellingcat's queries with legal threats, citing Colombian data protection laws, but did not answer questions.
- Bellingcat and Cerosetenta consulted legal experts and determined their reporting is protected by freedom of expression.
- They cited public interest and the subjects' status as 'public figures' as justification for their reporting. ## International Neo-Nazi Network Links
- The investigation suggests Active Club Bogota has links to international neo-Nazi networks Blood & Honour and Combat 18.
- There is no evidence connecting Rodriguez directly to Blood & Honour or Combat 18.
- Evidence includes a May 2024 photo of a man with Ruiz's tattoos next to Blood & Honour musician Ken McLellan in Bogota.
- Another associate sent gifts (including an Active Club Bogota sticker) to the alleged leader of Combat 18 in Spain.
- A neo-Nazi fashion retailer listing Ruiz as a contact was banned from WhatsApp by Meta after Bellingcat reached out.
- Combat 18 is designated a terrorist organization in Canada and is subject to UK financial sanctions.

## Brief
Dendron (dendronhq/dendron) is an open-source, local-first, markdown-based Personal Knowledge Management (PKM) tool built primarily with TypeScript, JavaScript, and HTML, also leveraging Next.js for publishing. It organizes knowledge in plaintext files within git-backed "vaults" and integrates with VS Code and VSCodium. Users interact with it through its VS Code integration and a CLI, which includes the `/sub` interface. The project is currently in maintenance-only mode.

## Detailed
## Overview
- Dendron's architecture centers on plaintext markdown files, managed with Git, and organized into "vaults." Dendron's design uses plaintext markdown stored in Git as vaults for organization. The system architecture is built around markdown files in Git-managed vaults. It extends markdown with "gradual structure" primitives and uses schemas for consistency. ### Core argument
- Dendron's architecture centers on plaintext markdown files, managed with Git, and organized into "vaults." Dendron's design uses plaintext markdown stored in Git as vaults for organization. The system architecture is built around markdown files in Git-managed vaults. It extends markdown with "gradual structure" primitives and uses schemas for consistency. ### Architecture
- Navigation is supported through backlinks and a graph view.
- The system provides robust refactoring capabilities and supports rich content like mermaid diagrams and KaTeX.
- Vaults can be published as static Next.js websites. ### Stack
- TypeScript, JavaScript, HTML, Next.js. ## Features and modules ### Overview
- Dendron is an open-source, local-first, markdown-based Personal Knowledge Management (PKM) tool.
- It is designed for developers and integrates with VS Code and VSCodium.
- The project is in maintenance-only mode; active development has ceased.
- Dendron's mission is to manage any amount of knowledge, aiming to scale beyond 10,000 notes.
- Its design is developer-centric, targeting the efficiency of Vim and extensibility of Emacs within a text-centric, keyboard-focused UX.
- It employs a principle of "gradual structure", extending markdown with primitives that can be added as a knowledge base grows.
- Public surface: /sub.
- Usability signals: Integrates with VS Code and VSCodium, Licensed under Apache 2.0. ### Architecture / Modules
- The architecture uses plaintext files manageable with git.
- Knowledge is organized into "vaults" (git-backed folders).
- Key features include a unified lookup for finding/creating notes.
- Schemas are used for consistency and autocompletion.
- Navigation is supported via backlinks and a graph view.
- Robust refactoring capabilities are provided, preserving links.
- Supports mermaid diagrams and KaTeX for math.
- Supports note embedding.
- Vaults can be published as static Next.js websites with granular permissions. ### Public API / Interfaces
- The CLI includes the `/sub` interface.
- Public surface: /sub. ### Operational guidance
- The repository provides a `./setup.sh` script for development environment automation.
- Usability signals:./setup.sh. ### Current Status / Issues
- The project is in maintenance-only mode, and active development has ceased.
- Recent issues involve bugs with Mermaid support overriding VS Code's native feature.
- Outdated documentation has been noted.
- CLI errors have been reported.
- Problems with image pasting and preview rendering have been observed. ## Closing remarks
- Roadmap: The project is currently in maintenance-only mode.
